TIME-OF-HIRE WORKERS' COMPENSATION RIGHTS NOTICE — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme, Inc.

PURPOSE OF THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's statutory requirement that an employer give a new employee, at the time of hire or by the end of the first pay period, written notice of information about workers' compensation benefits — including how to obtain treatment and how the claims process works — as set out in California Labor Code § 3551 and, by incorporation, § 3550. It is prepared in connection with Acme, Inc. and Jordan Lee, hired effective September 15, 2026.

This time-of-hire written notice is a different document from two other pamphlets and notices this corpus separately addresses. It is not the workplace-posted notice that Labor Code § 3550 also requires an employer to keep conspicuously posted (a companion, but separately-timed and separately-displayed, obligation described in this information sheet only to the extent § 3551 incorporates its content). It is also not the Employment Development Department's unemployment-insurance pamphlet ("For Your Benefit: California's Programs for the Unemployed," EDD form DE 2320) that a different California statute requires an employer to give a departing employee at separation — that is a distinct pamphlet, required by a different statute (Unemployment Insurance Code § 1089), addressing different benefits (unemployment insurance, not workers' compensation), given at a different time (termination, not hire), and is covered by this corpus's separate "Notice to Employee as to Change in Relationship" document. This information sheet does not determine whether Acme, Inc. has in fact provided this notice to Jordan Lee, does not determine whether any specific workplace injury is compensable, and is not a substitute for the actual text of the statutes and regulations it describes.

THE TIME-OF-HIRE WRITTEN NOTICE DUTY
California Labor Code § 3551(a) requires every employer subject to the compensation provisions of the Labor Code, with one statutory exception, to give every new employee — either at the time the employee is hired or by the end of the first pay period — written notice of the information contained in Labor Code § 3550. The statutory exception is for employers of employees defined in Labor Code § 3351(d). The content of this notice is prescribed by the Administrative Director (within the Department of Industrial Relations) after consultation with the Commission on Health and Safety and Workers' Compensation, not by the text of § 3551 itself.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Every employer subject to the compensation provisions of this code, except employers of employees defined in subdivision (d) of Section 3351, shall give every new employee, either at the time the employee is hired or by the end of the first pay period, written notice of the information contained in Section 3550."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3551, subd. (a) (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 3551(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3551.)
  "The content of the notice required by this section shall be prescribed by the administrative director after consultation with the Commission on Health and Safety and Workers’ Compensation."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3551, subd. (a) (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 3551(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3551.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, stating a fact about what California law requires of a covered employer generally at the time a new employee is hired — not a claim about whether any specific employer has in fact provided this notice to any specific employee, or about whether that employee falls within the § 3351(d) exception, which this document does not independently research. A CourtListener case-law search for judicial decisions construing this notice duty could not be completed this session because CourtListener's daily search quota (125/day) was already exhausted when checked (the API returned an HTTP 429 quota-exceeded response); rather than wait for the quota to reset, this document proceeds on the statutory and regulatory text alone and discloses that no case-law search was performed.

ADDITIONAL REQUIRED CONTENT AND THE BILINGUAL REQUIREMENT
Labor Code § 3551(b) requires the time-of-hire notice to be easily understandable and available in both English and Spanish, and requires it to include — beyond the information already contained in § 3550 — three further items: (1) generally, how to obtain appropriate medical care for a job injury; (2) the role and function of the primary treating physician; and (3) a form the employee may use as an optional method of notifying the employer of the name of the employee's "personal physician" (as defined by Labor Code § 4600) or "personal chiropractor" (as defined by Labor Code § 4601). Section 3551(c) further requires that the content of this notice be made available to employers and insurers by the administrative director, and requires insurers to provide the notice to each of their policyholders along with advice about the requirements of the section and the penalties for a failure to provide it to all employees.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "The notice required by this section shall be easily understandable and available in both English and Spanish."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3551, subd. (b) (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 3551(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3551.)
  "A form that the employee may use as an optional method for notifying the employer of the name of the employee’s “personal physician,” as defined by Section 4600, or “personal chiropractor,” as defined by Section 4601."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3551, subd. (b) (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 3551(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3551.)
  "Insurers shall provide this notice to each of their policyholders, with advice concerning the requirements of this section and the penalties for a failure to provide this notice to all employees."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3551, subd. (c) (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 3551(c) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3551.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, stating a fact about what content California law requires this notice to contain — not a claim about the content of any specific notice a specific employer has actually used, and not a restatement of the § 3550 content this section incorporates by reference, which is addressed in a separate clause of this information sheet. The statute's text does not itself spell out what "penalties" it refers to in subdivision (c); this document does not locate a separate penalty provision specific to a § 3551 violation and discloses that gap rather than assuming one.

THE INCORPORATED § 3550 CONTENT
Because Labor Code § 3551 requires the time-of-hire notice to contain "the information contained in Section 3550," the substantive list set out in § 3550(d) is, by that cross-reference, also part of what the time-of-hire notice must cover. That list includes: how to get emergency medical treatment if needed; the kinds of events, injuries, and illnesses covered by workers' compensation; the injured employee's right to receive medical care; that the injured employee may consult a licensed attorney, with attorney's fees in most instances paid from the employee's recovery; the employee's rights to select and change the treating physician under Labor Code § 4600; the employee's rights to receive temporary disability, permanent disability, supplemental job displacement, and death benefits as appropriate; to whom injuries should be reported; the existence of time limits for notifying the employer of an occupational injury; the anti-discrimination protections of Labor Code § 132a; and the internet website address and contact information (including the nearest information and assistance officer) employees may use to learn more about the claims process and their rights and obligations.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "(1) How to get emergency medical treatment, if needed."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3550, subd. (d) (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 3550(d) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3550.)
  "(4) The injured employee may consult a licensed attorney to advise them of their rights under workers’ compensations laws. In most instances, attorney’s fees will be paid from an injured employee’s recovery."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3550, subd. (d) (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 3550(d) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3550.)
  "(10) The internet website address and contact information that employees may use to obtain further information about the workers’ compensation claims process and an injured employee’s rights and obligations, including the location and telephone number of the nearest information and assistance officer."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3550, subd. (d) (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 3550(d) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3550.)
  "written notice of the information contained in Section 3550"
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3551, subd. (a) (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 3551(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3551.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, stating a fact about the content California law requires this incorporated list to cover — not a claim about the content of any specific notice a specific employer has actually used. Section 3550 (and therefore this incorporated list) was last amended effective January 1, 2025 (Stats. 2024, Ch. 87 (AB 1870)); this document reflects the version in effect as of the checked date above and does not attempt to reconstruct what the list read before that amendment. Section 3550's own posted-notice duty, and the separate misdemeanor and treat-with-personal-physician consequences that attach to a failure to keep that specific posted notice displayed, are addressed in a separate clause of this information sheet and are not restated here.

THE SEPARATE, WORKPLACE-POSTED NOTICE UNDER § 3550
Independent of the time-of-hire written notice, Labor Code § 3550(a) separately requires every employer subject to the compensation provisions to post and keep posted, in a conspicuous location frequented by employees where it may be easily read during the hours of the workday, a notice stating the name of the employer's current compensation insurance carrier (or that the employer is self-insured) and who is responsible for claims adjustment. Section 3550(b) makes a failure to keep this posted notice conspicuously displayed a misdemeanor and prima facie evidence of noninsurance, and § 3550(e) provides that an employer's failure to provide the notice required by that section automatically permits the employee to be treated by their own personal physician for an injury occurring during the failure.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Every employer subject to the compensation provisions of this division shall post and keep posted in a conspicuous location frequented by employees, and where the notice may be easily read by employees during the hours of the workday, a notice that states the name of the current compensation insurance carrier of the employer, or when appropriate, that the employer is self-insured, and who is responsible for claims adjustment."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3550, subd. (a) (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 3550(a) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3550.)
  "Failure to keep any notice required by this section conspicuously posted shall constitute a misdemeanor, and shall be prima facie evidence of noninsurance."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3550, subd. (b) (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 3550(b) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3550.)
  "Failure of an employer to provide the notice required by this section shall automatically permit the employee to be treated by their personal physician with respect to an injury occurring during that failure."
  — Cal. Labor Code § 3550, subd. (e) (California Legislative Information text), Lab. Code § 3550(e) (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=LAB&sectionNum=3550.)
  Known gap: This is one state's statute, stating a fact about a workplace-posting duty that exists alongside, but is legally and operationally distinct from, the time-of-hire written notice this information sheet centers on — not a claim about whether any specific employer has in fact posted this notice or which insurance carrier or self-insurance status any such posting states. The misdemeanor penalty and personal-physician consequence in subdivisions (b) and (e) attach to the posted-notice duty in § 3550 itself; § 3551 does not, by its own text, say that the same misdemeanor penalty or personal-physician consequence also attaches to a failure to give the separate time-of-hire notice, and this document does not assume that it does.

THE IMPLEMENTING REGULATION'S WRITTEN-NOTICE CONTENT LIST
The Administrative Director's implementing regulation for the time-of-hire notice, Title 8, California Code of Regulations § 9880, restates the § 3551 duty and lists the notice's required content in non-technical terms — including, among other items, the name of the employer's current compensation insurance carrier or self-insured status and claims-adjustment contact, how to get emergency medical treatment, the kinds of events and injuries covered, the employee's right to receive medical care, the role and function of the primary treating physician, the employee's rights to select and change the treating physician and to predesignate a personal physician or medical group, an optional personal-physician or personal-chiropractor notification form, disability and death benefit rights, reporting and time-limit information, the § 132a anti-discrimination protections, information-and-assistance officer contact information, and a description of medical provider networks (MPNs).

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Every employer shall provide to every new employee, either at the time of hire or by the end of the first pay period, the Written Notice to New Employees concerning the rights, benefits and obligations under worker's compensation law. The content of the notice must be approved by the Administrative Director."
  — Cal. Code Regs. tit. 8, § 9880 (Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School, secondary compilation of California Code of Regulations text), 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 9880 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/8-CCR-9880)
  "A description about Medical Provider Networks ("MPN") which includes that the employer may be using a MPN, what a MPN is, the predesignation exemption from the MPN, when an employee must begin to use a physician from the MPN, and how to request information about using a MPN."
  — Cal. Code Regs. tit. 8, § 9880 (Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School, secondary compilation of California Code of Regulations text), 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 9880 (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/8-CCR-9880)
  Known gap: This regulation's text could not be independently fetched from a primary California source this session: California regulations are not on eCFR, this project's usual leginfo-style approach does not host full current CCR text, and the Office of Administrative Law's own published-text search and Westlaw's govt.westlaw.com/calregs (the government's designated official publisher of the CCR) were not reachable from this environment; www.dir.ca.gov's own title-8 regulation pages (e.g., dir.ca.gov/title8/9880.html) returned HTTP 404 when fetched directly. The text quoted here instead comes from the Legal Information Institute (Cornell Law School)'s secondary compilation of Title 8 CCR § 9880, fetched twice with distinct User-Agent strings and confirmed byte-identical between the two fetches; LII is a well-established secondary legal-research compiler, not the primary California state publisher, and this document was not able to independently cross-check its text against an official OAL or Westlaw source this session. LII's own regulatory-history notes for this section show it was last substantively amended effective October 8, 2010 (Register 2010, No. 33); this document reflects that version and does not claim to have checked for any more recent amendment beyond what LII's own "updated quarterly" comparison shows (which found no more recent version).

EMPLOYER- OR INSURER-PUBLISHED VERSIONS OF THE NOTICE
Title 8, California Code of Regulations § 9883 allows insurers, employers, or private enterprises to prepare and publish their own version of the Written Notice to New Employees (and of the separate Notice to Employees poster) for their own use or for sale, but only upon prior approval of the form and content by the Administrative Director, and any such published Written Notice to New Employees must be available in English and Spanish and include the information specified in § 9880. A logotype may be added to a previously approved notice without requiring additional approval, and material published after the regulation's effective date must indicate that it has been approved by the Administrative Director.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-06]
  "Insurers, employers or private enterprises may prepare and publish for their use or sale the Notice to Employees poster and/or the Written Notice to New Employees required by this Article upon prior approval of the form and content by the Administrative Director."
  — Cal. Code Regs. tit. 8, § 9883, subd. (a) (Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School, secondary compilation of California Code of Regulations text), 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 9883(a) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/8-CCR-9883)
  "Any published Written Notice to New Employees shall be available in English and Spanish and shall include the information specified in Section 9880."
  — Cal. Code Regs. tit. 8, § 9883, subd. (a)(1) (Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School, secondary compilation of California Code of Regulations text), 8 Cal. Code Regs. § 9883(a)(1) (https://www.law.cornell.edu/regulations/california/8-CCR-9883)
  Known gap: As with the preceding clause, this regulation's text comes from the Legal Information Institute's secondary compilation, not from a primary California source independently verified this session, for the reasons disclosed there. This is one state's regulation, stating a fact about what California law permits an employer or insurer to do when publishing its own version of this notice — not a claim about whether any specific version a specific employer has used has, in fact, received the Administrative Director's prior approval, which this document does not investigate.

This is one state's regulation, stating a fact about what California law permits an employer or insurer to do when publishing its own version of this notice — not a claim about whether any specific version a specific employer has used has, in fact, received the Administrative Director's prior approval, which this document does not investigate.
